items.title: 67619_Big Nick Nicholas oral history interview
items.q: he worked with Earl Bostic and played tenor with him

ctx.x: Red Garland and Philly Joe Jones and John Acee, who was from Philadelphia, and Coltrane was around there (Phil.) for many years. And he used to sit up under me and look at me and he never said nothing. So I says, "Acee, who is that?" He says, "That's John Coltrane," he says, "He plays alto. He plays like Bird." I says, "Yeah?" He says, "Man, he's next to bird."

Then I didn't know at that time that...later on, then I didn't see him anymore. But then I found out that he went with Johnny Hodges and played tenor with him and he worked with Earl Bostic and played tenor with him, learning all the time. And he studied everybody. But I didn't know he was really listening to me.
I guess he was listening to you enough at the time to have warranted his naming quite a well known tune after you.
